caption: The drawing depicts a stone doorway or archway set into a rough stone wall. The doorway is constructed from large, light gray stone blocks, forming an arched top with some decorative elements, including carved column-like structures on either side of the opening. The arch itself consists of several fitted stone segments, some with carved details, and a keystone at the top center adorned with a relief. The inner portion of the doorway is completely filled in with small, irregularly shaped, reddish-brown bricks that are stacked closely together, effectively blocking what might once have been a passage. Surrounding the doorway, the wall is made of larger, irregular, and roughly cut pale stones, giving a weathered appearance. The composition centers the doorway on the page with a plain, off-white background, and there is a shadowed floor area at the bottom suggesting depth. The overall color palette includes grays, browns, and hints of reddish tones in the bricks.
title: Stone Doorway, Carved
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
